chunks.arabic_text: شَرِيفُ بْنُ سَابِقٍ، التِّفْلِسِيُّ، أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ. رَوَى عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ أَبِي قُرَّةَ السَّهَنْدِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: Sharīf ibn Sābiq, al-Taflīsī, Abū Muḥammad. He narrated from al-Faḍl ibn Abī Qurra al-Sahandī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him).
He is weak, confused in the affair.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* identifies Sharīf ibn Sābiq al-Taflīsī as a narrator in the chain leading to Imam al-Ṣādiq (AS), specifically through al-Faḍl ibn Abī Qurra. He is classified as *ḍaʿīf* (weak) and *muḍarib al-amr* (erratic or confused), indicating inconsistencies in his memory or reliability that scholars weigh when assessing the authenticity of transmitted hadiths.
en.seo_question: Who is Sharīf ibn Sābiq al-Taflīsī and what is his status in hadith sciences?

key_terms.شَرِيفُ بْنُ سَابِقٍ: Sharīf ibn Sābiq, the narrator's name
key_terms.الْفَضْلِ بْنِ أَبِي قُرَّةَ: al-Faḍl ibn Abī Qurra, the intermediate narrator
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, referring to Imam al-Sādiq (AS)
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak, a technical term for a narrator whose reliability is questionable
key_terms.مُضْطَرِبُ الْأَمْرِ: Confused/erratic in affairs, indicating inconsistency or confusion in narration
